newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shrs end lower, unaffected by U.S. chip data.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shrs end lower, unaffected by U.S. chip data.

text.p: Seoul stocks closed Wednesday's thin trading a fraction lower after investors' hopes that the market would be boosted by improved U.S. semiconductor data fizzled out, brokers said.

The market opened firm on the rise of Samsung Electronics, bolstered by the U.S. Semiconductor Industry Association's announcement that the book-to-bill ratio increased to 0.9 in August from a revised 0.86 in July. But it fell on immediate profit-taking.
The composite stock index lost 1.59 points lower to provisionally close at 801.45.
Samsung Electronics shed 200 won to 60,100, after moving in a 59,200-61,300 won range. It hit today's top 10 trading volume with 191,770 shares changing hands.
LG Electroncis, which holds more than a 50 percent stake in unlisted LG Semicon, closed flat at 14,800.

"The ratio rise was not caused by a recovery in the semiconductor market, but by a cut in output by chipmakers," said Kim Duck-sun of Hyundai Securities. "Profit-takers tried to materialise their quick gains."
"The market engergy is not enough to lift many large-cap shares," said Lee Yon-suk of Citicorp International.
Lee said rotational buying interest moved to small-caps backed by themes, asset-rich issues and second-tier shares.
Both Mon Ami and Silla Trading went limit up, gaining 1,200 won to 22,000, and 3,100 won to 56,400, respectively.

Analysts said concerns about possible heavy selling pressure from margin account holders depressed the market. Outstanding margin accounts are currently at an all-time high of 2.68 trillion won, they said. The index is likely to move below the psychologically important 800 level as a recent technical rebound appeared to be waning, analysts added.
